paragraphs: Natural gradient descent can offer favorable convergence behavior, but computing the information needed for its updates is expensive. This paper introduces LNGD, a layer-wise optimizer that reduces that expense by approximating the Fisher information matrix. The aim is to retain useful information for choosing updates while making training more practical.

The method starts with a block diagonal approximation and computes the blocks using layer-wise sampling, without requiring a complete backward pass for each block. It then replaces each block with a Kronecker product of two smaller matrices, one diagonal. This approximation preserves the block’s trace, giving the compression a specific mathematical constraint rather than simply discarding entries.

LNGD also adjusts learning rates separately by layer to accelerate training. The authors establish a global convergence analysis under assumptions and report competitive results on image classification and machine translation. Together, these contributions address both the cost of constructing natural gradient updates and the choice of update size, with empirical support across two different kinds of learning tasks.
neurips-2024-a-layer-wise-natural-gradie.tldr: LNGD makes natural gradient training cheaper through layer-wise Fisher approximations and adaptive learning rates, with competitive results on classification and translation.

paragraphs: Testing the robustness of tabular models requires attacks that respect the structure of their inputs. Categories, unchangeable attributes, and relationships between features restrict which changes are valid. This paper develops attacks for that setting, addressing weaknesses in existing methods that can leave deep tabular models insufficiently tested.

The first contribution, CAPGD, uses adaptive mechanisms to improve gradient-based attacks without parameter tuning. The authors report accuracy reductions of up to 81 percentage points beyond previous gradient attacks. They then combine CAPGD with MOEVA, a search-based attack, to create CAA. The combination brings two attack approaches into a single robustness evaluation method.

Across five architectures and four use cases, CAA outperforms existing attacks in 17 of 20 settings. Reported accuracy drops reach up to 96.1 percentage points relative to CAPGD and 21.9 relative to MOEVA, while CAA is up to five times faster than MOEVA. These empirical results motivate the authors’ proposal that the attacks serve as a minimum evaluation for new tabular defenses and robust architectures.
neurips-2024-constrained-adaptive-attack.tldr: CAA combines adaptive gradient and search-based attacks to expose weaknesses in deep tabular models while respecting their input constraints.

paragraphs: Intracranial EEG signals differ substantially between people, making seizure detectors difficult to transfer across subjects. This paper investigates that failure and identifies a shared pattern: seizure events have higher average amplitude than nearby normal events. The proposed approach uses this relative change as a basis for detection across differing signal conditions.

DMNet compares signals against two constructed references, one contextual and one at the channel level. These self-comparisons aim to reduce differences across subjects and time intervals while preserving seizure-related changes. A difference matrix encodes the resulting patterns, giving the network a representation centered on changes relative to references rather than relying only on the original signals.

Experiments on an author-collected clinical dataset and two public datasets show significant improvements over previous leading methods while maintaining high efficiency. Visualizations indicate that the difference matrices capture changes as seizures evolve. The authors also deploy DMNet in an online diagnosis system to illustrate its clinical applicability. The findings support self-comparison as a useful mechanism for subject-independent detection in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-dmnet-self-comparison-drive.tldr: DMNet uses signal self-comparisons and difference matrices to improve seizure detection across subjects with differing intracranial EEG patterns.

paragraphs: Video transformers process large token sequences even when portions of successive frames repeat. Run-Length Tokenization, or RLT, reduces this redundancy before the model processes the video. Its motivation is straightforward: repeated visual content creates computational work without necessarily providing equally much new information.

RLT finds runs of patches that repeat over time and replaces each run with one patch. A positional encoding records the resulting token’s duration, preserving information about how long the content persists. The procedure adapts to video content without dataset-specific tuning and adds negligible overhead, addressing a problem with token-removal methods whose own processing can consume the expected savings.

The reported experiments reduce video-transformer fine-tuning time by 30% while matching baseline performance. Applied without training, RLT increases throughput by 35% with a reported accuracy drop of only 0.1%. On longer videos, token reductions reach 80%. These results show that temporal repetition can be exploited at the input stage to improve efficiency, with the reported gains varying across the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-don-t-look-twice-faster-vid.tldr: RLT compresses repeated video patches into duration-aware tokens, reducing fine-tuning time by 30% while matching baseline performance in reported experiments.

paragraphs: CLIP learns useful connections between images and language, but its understanding of local visual details can be weak. That creates problems for dense prediction tasks, which need information about particular parts of an image. FineCLIP aims to improve those local representations while preserving consistency between overall visual content and its meaning in language.

The method retains global contrastive learning and adds two cooperating components. A real-time self-distillation scheme transfers representation capability from global features to local features. Regional contrastive learning also uses generated region-text pairs, supplying semantic information tied to image regions. Together, these components let local features draw on both the model’s global understanding and more specific regional supervision.

The authors evaluate FineCLIP on challenging dense prediction tasks and image-level tasks, reporting evidence for the method’s effectiveness and its individual design choices. The contribution is therefore a training approach that connects learning at multiple visual scales. Its stated findings support improving fine-grained understanding without abandoning the global image-language relationship that makes CLIP useful.
neurips-2024-fineclip-self-distilled-reg.tldr: FineCLIP combines global learning, self-distillation, and region-text training to strengthen local visual understanding while preserving image-language consistency.

paragraphs: Reconstructing transparent and opaque objects together is difficult for existing methods that infer three-dimensional shape from multiple images. This paper introduces alpha-NeuS, an extension of NeuS, and establishes that NeuS is unbiased across materials ranging from fully transparent to fully opaque. It then examines how different surfaces appear in the learned distance field.

The key distinction concerns where surfaces are represented. Opaque surfaces correspond to the field’s zero iso-surface, while transparent surfaces correspond to non-negative local minima. A method that extracts only one fixed field value can therefore be poorly matched to the representation. The issue involves how geometry is extracted from the field, as well as what the field has learned.

The authors develop a surface extraction method based on DCUDF that handles transparent and opaque surfaces together. They also construct a benchmark containing synthetic and real-world scenes to evaluate the approach, reporting practical effectiveness. The work connects a mathematical interpretation of the learned field to an extraction procedure designed for scenes containing both material types.
neurips-2024-from-transparent-to-opaque-.tldr: Alpha-NeuS explains how transparent and opaque surfaces occupy a learned distance field and extracts both with a method tailored to that structure.

paragraphs: One-shot federated learning reduces communication by aggregating trained models only once, but its performance can lag behind ordinary federated learning. This paper analyzes that gap through a causal perspective. It identifies isolation during local training as a problem: clients with differing data may learn spurious relationships that do not transfer well.

The authors observe that augmenting intermediate features with features from other clients can alleviate this spurious fitting. FuseFL implements that idea by dividing networks into blocks, then progressively training and fusing those blocks from the bottom upward. Feature augmentation is therefore built into the model’s development, with the method introducing no additional communication costs according to the abstract.

Experiments show substantial improvements over existing one-shot and ensemble federated learning methods. They also demonstrate support for many clients, heterogeneous models, and low memory costs. These findings connect the proposed explanation of the performance gap to a concrete intervention: giving local learning access to richer intermediate representations can reduce the effects of training in isolation.
neurips-2024-fusefl-one-shot-federated-l.tldr: FuseFL progressively fuses network blocks to share intermediate features and reduce spurious fitting in one-shot federated learning.

paragraphs: This paper develops forest-based generative models for tabular data. Its central contribution combines a new model class with a simple training algorithm supported by strong convergence guarantees in a boosting framework. The learning setup parallels the relationship between weak and strong learners in supervised learning.

A practical feature is that training can be implemented through a few changes to a commonly used decision-tree induction procedure for two-class classification. The model structure and training losses also support fast density estimation for observations that may be only partly specified. That makes the same generative framework useful for estimating data densities and filling in missing values.

Experiments report substantial improvements in generated-data quality over the state of the art. Further evaluations find the models competitive for imputation and density estimation against diverse approaches involving trees, neural networks, kernels, and graphical models. The work therefore presents forests as a versatile generative tool, with both theoretical training support and empirical evidence extending beyond the generation task itself.
neurips-2024-generative-forests-229e1aef.tldr: Generative Forests adapts decision-tree training into a theoretically supported approach for tabular generation, density estimation, and missing-data imputation.

paragraphs: GTBench evaluates language models through competitive games that require logical and strategic decisions. Its language-driven environment includes ten recognized tasks spanning different information conditions, decision structures, and degrees of randomness. This range lets the authors investigate how reasoning behavior changes with the kind of game being played.

The study combines analysis of model behavior with competitions between models. In the evaluated settings, models struggle in games with complete information and deterministic outcomes but are competitive in probabilistic games. Most tested open-source models trail commercial models in complex games, although Llama-3-70b-Instruct closes that gap. These results show a varied performance profile rather than a single uniform level of strategic ability.

The authors also report that code pretraining strongly benefits strategic reasoning, while Chain-of-Thought and Tree-of-Thought do not consistently help. Additional analyses examine equilibrium and Pareto efficiency in repeated games and provide detailed error profiles. GTBench thus supplies an evaluation protocol and behavioral evidence for studying which aspects of competitive reasoning current models handle successfully.
neurips-2024-gtbench-uncovering-the-stra.tldr: GTBench uses ten competitive games to reveal uneven strategic reasoning in LLMs and shows that advanced prompting methods do not consistently improve performance.

paragraphs: A transformer’s ability to represent a computation does not establish that it can efficiently learn that computation from examples. This paper introduces the globality degree of a target distribution to study that distinction. The measure concerns when ordinary transformers can efficiently achieve weak learning, connecting learnability to a more restricted computational class than expressivity analyses consider.

The authors present experimental evidence and theoretical results under additional assumptions that high-globality distributions cannot be learned efficiently. Long chains of syllogistic composition illustrate the barrier. They then examine scratchpads, which provide intermediate reasoning steps, and find that agnostic scratchpads cannot overcome it. Educated scratchpads can, although some still fail to generalize outside the training distribution.

The proposed inductive scratchpads compose prior information more efficiently and can both overcome the barrier and improve out-of-distribution generalization. Some achieve length generalization up to six times longer on certain arithmetic tasks, depending on input formatting. The results make the organization of intermediate reasoning central to learnability, while keeping the strongest generalization claims tied to particular tasks and formats.
neurips-2024-how-far-can-transformers-re.tldr: The paper identifies a conditional learnability barrier for transformers and develops inductive scratchpads that can overcome it and improve length generalization.

paragraphs: M³GPT brings motion understanding and generation into a shared framework that accepts multiple types of signals. It connects text, music, and motion or dance through a unified representation space. Discrete vector quantization turns the conditioning signals into a shared vocabulary that can be integrated into a large language model.

The framework makes a separate choice for generating motion: it models output directly in the raw motion space. This avoids the information loss associated with representing generated motion through a discrete tokenizer and supports more detailed motion output. The distinction between compact conditioning inputs and direct motion generation is one of the design’s central principles.

M³GPT also uses text to connect motion-related tasks, drawing on language models’ familiarity with that modality to encourage mutual reinforcement. Experiments report strong performance across multiple motion tasks and substantial zero-shot generalization on challenging tasks. The findings support combining representations and task relationships within one system, while preserving motion detail through the choice of output space.
neurips-2024-m-3-gpt-an-advanced-multimo.tldr: M³GPT unifies multimodal motion tasks through a shared input vocabulary, text-based task connections, and generation directly in raw motion space.

paragraphs: Universal Transformers reuse parameters across layers, allowing repeated computation through depth and supporting compositional generalization. That sharing also sharply reduces parameter count compared with a standard transformer of the same dimensionality. Simply widening shared layers to restore capacity can make computation prohibitively expensive, creating a practical obstacle for language modeling.

MoEUT addresses this parameter-to-compute tradeoff with a mixture-of-experts architecture for shared-layer transformers. It combines expert-based developments in both feedforward and attention layers with new normalization and grouping schemes designed specifically for Universal Transformers. The abstract identifies these additional schemes as crucial, making the contribution a coordinated architecture rather than only the addition of experts.

In the reported evaluations, including BLiMP and PIQA, MoEUT slightly outperforms standard transformers while using substantially less computation and memory. The performance improvement is modest, but it comes alongside meaningful resource savings. These findings demonstrate that shared-layer models can be competitive in tasks where parameter capacity matters, addressing a practical weakness that had limited earlier Universal Transformer designs.
neurips-2024-moeut-mixture-of-experts-un.tldr: MoEUT combines expert layers with specialized sharing schemes to slightly outperform standard transformers in reported evaluations while reducing compute and memory.

paragraphs: Blockchain analysis involves relationships at more than one level: transactions occur within tokens, while tokens also interact across platforms. This paper introduces datasets designed to represent both levels together. It addresses the lack of large-scale cross-chain data with hierarchical graph information and detailed labels at the token level.

The proposed Graphs of Graphs representation treats transactions within each token as a local graph. Relationships among tokens form a global graph whose components carry their own internal structure. Combining these views makes it possible to study token-level activity alongside broader interactions, preserving information that belongs to different levels of the system.

The authors conduct experiments showing that the datasets create new insights and research challenges for hierarchical blockchain analysis. They identify link prediction, anomaly detection, and token classification as relevant applications. The main contribution is therefore a data resource and representation approach for studying systemic structure, providing a basis for research that connects local transaction patterns with relationships across tokens and chains.
neurips-2024-multi-chain-graphs-of-graph.tldr: The paper introduces cross-chain blockchain datasets that connect local transaction graphs through a global graph of token relationships.

paragraphs: This paper studies distributed convex-concave minimax optimization when objectives across nodes satisfy a second-order similarity condition. The challenge involves several costs at once: synchronization rounds, total communication, and local gradient computations. Its proposed method, SVOGS, uses the objective’s finite-sum structure to improve these costs together.

SVOGS combines optimistic gradient sliding with variance reduction and mini-batch client sampling. For an epsilon duality gap, the authors prove a communication-round bound of O(delta D²/epsilon) and total communication of O(n + √n delta D²/epsilon). Here, n counts nodes, delta measures second-order similarity, and D is the constraint-set diameter. The local gradient bound additionally depends on the smoothness parameter.

The reported bounds match or nearly match corresponding lower bounds, making the theoretical efficiency claim specific to this problem setting. The authors also derive nearly tight bounds for a stronger special case involving a parameter mu, with logarithmic dependence on inverse accuracy in communication rounds. Numerical experiments support empirical advantages, complementing the analysis of communication and computation.
neurips-2024-near-optimal-distributed-mi.tldr: SVOGS exploits second-order similarity, client sampling, and variance reduction to achieve nearly optimal distributed minimax communication and computation bounds.

paragraphs: Visual tokenizers translate images or videos into compact representations for generative models. OmniTokenizer provides one transformer-based framework for both input types, addressing the separation between existing image and video tokenizers. The goal is to let spatial information from images and temporal information from videos contribute to a shared representation system.

Its architecture separates spatial and temporal modeling, using window attention for space and causal attention for time. Training also proceeds in stages. The tokenizer first learns spatial encoding from images at a fixed resolution, then trains jointly on images and videos at multiple resolutions to learn temporal dynamics and exploit their complementary information.

Experiments report leading reconstruction performance, including a reconstruction FID of 1.11 on ImageNet and reconstruction FVD of 42 on UCF-101. These improve on previous leading results by 13% and 26%, respectively. Integration with both language-model-based generators and diffusion models also produces strong visual synthesis results. The findings support a common tokenizer as a useful component across multiple visual generation approaches.
neurips-2024-omnitokenizer-a-joint-image.tldr: OmniTokenizer jointly encodes images and videos using separated spatial-temporal attention and progressive training, achieving strong reconstruction and generation results.

paragraphs: Preference-based alignment can be undermined when desirable and undesirable responses are assigned the wrong labels. PerpCorrect addresses these errors by correcting the training data. Its central signal is the perplexity difference between chosen and rejected responses, measured using an aligned surrogate language model.

The method first aligns the surrogate on clean validation data so that this difference can help distinguish reliable preferences from mislabeled ones. It then strengthens the surrogate using highly reliable training examples: pairs with extremely small differences are treated as clean, while pairs with extremely large differences are incorporated after correction. The refined surrogate subsequently identifies and corrects noise across the training dataset.

The intuition is probabilistic: a larger perplexity difference suggests a greater chance that the preference labels are wrong, because an aligned model should be less inclined to generate an undesirable response. Experiments report leading alignment performance under noisy preferences. The method requires a modest amount of clean validation data and works with multiple alignment techniques, making data correction a complementary route to improving robustness.
neurips-2024-perplexity-aware-correction.tldr: PerpCorrect uses an aligned surrogate model’s perplexity differences to detect and repair mislabeled preference pairs before alignment training.

paragraphs: Message-passing graph networks can struggle to move information across long distances or through narrow structural bottlenecks. Graph transformers offer another route, but their quadratic dependence on node count limits scalability. This paper proposes IPR-MPNNs to improve information flow while avoiding that quadratic cost.

The method adds a small number of virtual nodes and connects them to existing graph nodes through implicit probabilistic rewiring. These connections are learned differentiably as part of end-to-end training. The additional nodes provide routes for long-distance messages, allowing the network to change how information travels without requiring the costly interaction structure associated with graph transformers.

The authors prove that IPR-MPNNs are more expressive than traditional message-passing networks. Experiments show reduced under-reaching and over-squashing, alongside leading performance across multiple graph datasets. The evaluated models also outperform graph transformers while running substantially faster. Together, the theoretical and empirical results support learned virtual-node connectivity as a way to strengthen graph reasoning while retaining favorable computational efficiency.
neurips-2024-probabilistic-graph-rewirin.tldr: IPR-MPNNs learn virtual-node connections that improve long-range graph communication and expressiveness without quadratic computational complexity.

paragraphs: Distributed language-model training depends on both memory use and communication costs. This paper argues that existing basic training strategies leave useful options unexplored, especially when communication within a group differs from communication between groups. PaRO introduces strategies designed around those disparities and their effect on training speed.

PaRO Data Parallelism refines how model states are partitioned and pairs that partitioning with tailored training procedures. PaRO Collective Communications separately rearranges communication topology to accelerate collective operations. The authors also propose a quantitative guideline for selecting among data-parallel strategies, reporting small errors in how it ranks the available choices.

Experiments show substantial speed improvements over ZeRO-3 when comparing basic data-parallel strategies. PaRO’s communication component can also be used independently: applying it to model-parallel strategies such as Megatron improves training speed by 17% in the reported evaluation. The contribution therefore includes both a training strategy and a reusable communication technique, with results emphasizing the value of accounting for differences in communication performance.
neurips-2024-rethinking-memory-and-commu.tldr: PaRO accelerates distributed LLM training by coordinating model-state partitioning and communication topology with differences in communication costs.

paragraphs: Language models can write code to use tools, but embodied tasks also demand intricate logic and precise control. RL-GPT combines code-based policies with reinforcement learning to address these different needs. The paper’s motivation is that high-level planning lends itself to direct coding, while low-level actions often benefit from task-specific learning.

The framework organizes this combination through two agents operating at different levels. A slow agent analyzes which actions are suitable for coding, and a fast agent carries out the coding tasks. This division gives each agent a more focused responsibility within the overall pipeline, providing a structure for integrating planning through code with refinement through reinforcement learning.

The authors report greater efficiency than traditional reinforcement-learning methods and existing GPT agents. In Minecraft, the system obtains diamonds within a single day using an RTX3090, and it achieves leading performance across all designated MineDojo tasks. These results support the proposed decomposition in the evaluated environments, showing how coded planning and learned control can contribute within one framework.
neurips-2024-rl-gpt-integrating-reinforc.tldr: RL-GPT combines hierarchical coding agents with reinforcement learning to improve efficiency on embodied tasks, including Minecraft and designated MineDojo evaluations.

paragraphs: Density-based clustering becomes expensive when identifying core points and their neighborhoods in large, high-dimensional datasets. sDBSCAN targets this bottleneck for cosine distance using random projections. With a sufficiently large collection of random vectors, it can identify the relevant points and neighborhoods quickly.

The authors prove that sDBSCAN preserves DBSCAN’s clustering structure with high probability under mild conditions. They also introduce sOPTICS, a scalable visualization tool intended to guide parameter choices. Random kernel features extend both methods to several additional distances, including L2, L1, chi-squared, and Jensen-Shannon, broadening the range of data comparisons they can support.

On evaluated real-world datasets containing millions of points, sDBSCAN is significantly faster and more accurate than competing DBSCAN variants. Both proposed tools finish in minutes, whereas the compared implementations require hours or exceed the available memory. These results connect a conditional structural guarantee with substantial practical scalability gains, making neighborhood discovery the central target of the acceleration rather than changing the clustering objective.
neurips-2024-scalable-dbscan-with-random.tldr: sDBSCAN uses random projections to accelerate density-based clustering, with conditional structure-preservation guarantees and minute-scale results on million-point datasets.

paragraphs: This paper studies the quantum approximate optimization algorithm, QAOA, on the spiked tensor estimation problem. The setting is useful for examining quantum computational benefits because classical methods face a substantial gap between statistical possibility and computational tractability. The analysis asks when QAOA can recover information about the planted signal.

The authors prove that one-step QAOA has the same weak recovery threshold as one-step tensor power iteration. Heuristic calculations suggest the same correspondence for any fixed number of steps. Those calculations further suggest that multi-step QAOA combined with tensor unfolding could reach, but not exceed, the asymptotic classical computational threshold. This broader conclusion has a different evidential status from the one-step proof.

The paper also characterizes an asymptotic overlap distribution with a sine-Gaussian law, supported by simulations. For some step counts and tensor orders, QAOA has a constant-factor advantage in its effective recovery threshold. Thus, the results allow finite-factor benefits without establishing a better asymptotic scaling, and introduce Fourier-transform techniques for handling the combinatorial sums in the analysis.
neurips-2024-statistical-estimation-in-t.tldr: One-step QAOA matches a classical tensor method’s recovery threshold, while heuristic multi-step analysis suggests possible constant-factor benefits without better asymptotic scaling.

paragraphs: Some decisions in a reinforcement-learning policy matter much more for safety than others. This paper develops a model-based testing method that ranks states by their importance and concentrates evaluation on the most consequential decisions. The ranking covers the entire modeled state space, giving test selection a systematic basis.

At each iteration, the framework computes optimistic and pessimistic safety estimates that bound expected policy outcomes across modeled states. These bounds guide further testing and, upon convergence, divide the state space into safe and unsafe regions. The approach is designed to evaluate the states most critical for safety throughout the testing process.

A central result is that sampling only part of the policy can still provide formal guarantees across the modeled state space. Safety properties established by the pessimistic estimate are proven to hold for the policy. Evaluations on several examples find unsafe behavior with little testing effort. Although the paper focuses on safety, the authors state that the method can also be adapted to performance testing.
neurips-2024-test-where-decisions-matter.tldr: A model-based testing framework prioritizes safety-critical decisions and can establish formal policy guarantees from evaluating only a fraction of its behavior.

paragraphs: Different neural-network parameter settings can represent exactly the same function. These parameter symmetries are thought to influence phenomena such as model merging, connectivity between solutions, and Bayesian inference, but their effects are difficult to analyze theoretically. This paper studies them empirically by modifying networks to reduce their symmetries.

The authors introduce two modification methods with some provable guarantees, then use the resulting architectures across multiple tasks. Reducing symmetries provides a way to investigate how training behavior and relationships between learned solutions change when fewer equivalent parameter arrangements are available. The experimental design turns symmetry reduction into a practical tool for studying these questions.

Among the findings, the modified networks exhibit linear mode connectivity without first aligning their weight spaces. They also support faster and more effective Bayesian neural-network training. These observations show concrete consequences of the architectural changes and provide evidence about symmetry’s role in the evaluated phenomena. The contribution combines methods for reducing parameter symmetries with an empirical examination of what that reduction changes.
neurips-2024-the-empirical-impact-of-neu.tldr: The paper reduces neural parameter symmetries to study their empirical effects, finding connectivity without weight alignment and improved Bayesian network training.

paragraphs: Combining multiple modalities can improve sentiment analysis because each contributes complementary information. In practical settings, however, an uncertain subset of those inputs may be missing. HRLF addresses this situation by learning representations intended to preserve useful sentiment information despite incomplete multimodal input.

Its first component separates sentiment-relevant information from information specific to each modality. Crossmodal translation and reconstruction of sentiment semantics support that separation. A hierarchical mutual-information mechanism then increases shared information among representations at multiple scales, helping align and reconstruct their higher-level meaning. These stages aim to retain the semantic relationships that make multimodal fusion useful.

The framework also applies hierarchical adversarial learning to align and adapt the distributions of sentiment-relevant representations, producing a more robust joint representation. Experiments on three datasets show significant sentiment-analysis improvements under uncertain missing modalities. The contribution is a coordinated representation-learning approach: separating useful sentiment content, reconnecting it across scales, and aligning it across modalities all address different parts of the incomplete-input problem.
neurips-2024-toward-robust-incomplete-mu.tldr: HRLF combines representation factorization, information sharing, and adversarial alignment to improve sentiment analysis when modalities are unpredictably missing.

paragraphs: Large neural networks make multi-agent reinforcement learning computationally expensive. Dynamic sparse training offers a way to reduce that burden, but directly transferring it from supervised learning can disrupt value learning. This paper introduces MAST to make sparse networks more effective within value-based multi-agent methods.

MAST addresses both learning targets and the distribution of training examples. It combines the Soft Mellowmax Operator with a hybrid TD-lambda scheme to produce more dependable targets, and uses two replay buffers to improve the sample distribution. Gradient-based topology evolution then changes the sparse network structure during training, allowing agents to be trained using sparse networks throughout.

Across multiple value-based algorithms and benchmarks, the authors report up to a twentyfold reduction in floating-point operations for training and inference, with less than 3% performance degradation. The results indicate that sparsity can yield substantial computational savings when the learning process is adapted to support it. The method’s contribution is therefore both network compression and changes that help preserve reliable value learning under sparse computation.
neurips-2024-value-based-deep-multi-agen.tldr: MAST stabilizes sparse multi-agent value learning, reporting up to twentyfold FLOP reductions with less than 3% performance degradation.
